title: Portfolio Website Project Proposal
text:
Digital marketing project proposals

Personal Portfolio Brand Strategy

Data and source: My resume, coursework, portfolio content, and the requirements for this website.
Managerial problem: My marketing and analytics work needs to be organized in one place for job applications.
Target audience: Recruiters, hiring managers, professional contacts, etc.
Research questions and objectives: Decide which experiences to feature, how to organize the projects, and how to keep the tone and design consistent.
Expected impact: Make my background easier to understand and give visitors one place to review my work.
Methods: Content review, audience definition, basic SEO, and testing on different screen sizes.



Sirius Travel Content Strategy

Data and source: Public Sirius Travel website and social media content, plus examples of promotional materials I created.
Managerial problem: It can be difficult to explain both the trip and the astronomical event clearly to prospective travelers.
Target audience: Prospective travelers interested in astronomy, eclipse travel, and educational group experiences.
Research questions and objectives: Review content themes, message consistency, and how calls to action guide visitors toward more information.
Expected impact: Create a clearer and more consistent approach for presenting specialized tours.
Methods: Content review, audience segmentation, brand and message review, channel planning, and review of public engagement measures.

title: Portfolio Website Project Proposal
text:
Marketing analytics project proposals

Collins College CEP

Data and source: I plan to use de-identified Collins College data.
Managerial problem: Collins College needs a clearer view of student engagement patterns and how they may relate to enrollment and retention.
Target audience: Collins College administrators and the CEP team.
Research questions and objectives: Define the available engagement, enrollment, and retention measures and compare patterns over time or across available student groups.
Expected impact: Give Collins College a clearer summary of engagement patterns and identify questions for additional study.
Methods: Data cleaning, descriptive statistics, trend analysis, group comparisons, and data visualization.



Portfolio Website Traffic Analysis

Data and source: Google Analytics 4 and Google Search Console data from this portfolio, with Search Console linked to GA4, GA4 data sent to BigQuery, and results summarized in Looker Studio.
Managerial problem: I need to understand how visitors find and use the portfolio before I can improve it.
Target audience: Me as the site owner, along with prospective employers reviewing my analytics work.
Research questions and objectives: Compare traffic channels, page engagement, navigation paths, and possible areas for improvement.
Expected impact: Improve the portfolio’s content, navigation, and search visibility.
Methods: Traffic, page, device, trend, and conversion-event comparisons using BigQuery, Looker Studio, and Quarto.



Sirius Travel Revealjs Presentation

Data and source: Public Sirius Travel content and Google Trends search-interest data related to eclipses and astronomical tourism.
Managerial problem: The project will examine how public interest and engagement patterns can support decisions about what to post and when.
Target audience: Sirius Travel team members who plan content and promote tours.
Research questions and objectives: Compare search interest, public content themes, visible interaction, and posting timing.
Expected impact: Help the team plan content around periods of higher public interest.
Methods: Descriptive statistics, content comparisons, time-series visualization, and comparison of posting timing with search interest.

These are proposals, so I have not included results that have not been collected yet.

title: Using Public Data to Guide Sirius Travel Content
text:
Project overview
Project title: Using Public Data to Guide Sirius Travel Content
Project type: Marketing analytics and data visualization project
Status: This is a proposal, so I am not reporting results yet.



Why I chose it


This topic connects Sirius Travel’s public content with data I can collect and analyze in R.

title: Using Public Data to Guide Sirius Travel Content
text:
Data and source
I plan to use two public data sources:

Publicly visible content from the Sirius Travel website and company social media
Google Trends search-interest data for terms related to eclipses and astronomical tourism

title: Using Public Data to Guide Sirius Travel Content
text:
Public content dataset
I will organize a recent sample of public posts into a small dataset with:

Publication date and platform
Content theme, such as eclipse, destination, education, or tour information
Format, such as image, video, link, or text
Call to action
Visible reactions, comments, or shares when available

title: Using Public Data to Guide Sirius Travel Content
text:
Google Trends dataset
I will download weekly Google Trends data for a location and time period that match the public content sample.
Proposed search terms include:

Total solar eclipse
Eclipse tour
Astronomy travel

title: Using Public Data to Guide Sirius Travel Content
text:
Managerial problem
Sirius Travel offers specialized, science-focused tours. The project will look at how the company can explain the value of its trips, reach people when interest is higher, and stay consistent across channels.

title: Using Public Data to Guide Sirius Travel Content
text:
Target audience
This project is mainly for the Sirius Travel team members who plan content and promote tours.

title: Using Public Data to Guide Sirius Travel Content
text:
Research questions and objectives

How does public search interest in eclipses and astronomical travel change over time?
Which public content themes and formats receive the most visible interaction?
How closely does the timing of Sirius Travel content align with periods of higher search interest?
What content mix and timing should be considered for future tour promotion?

title: Using Public Data to Guide Sirius Travel Content
text:
Data preparation
I will:

Collect only public posts and search-interest data.
Standardize dates, platforms, themes, formats, and calls to action.
Record visible interactions consistently and mark missing values.
Check for duplicate posts and differences between platforms.
Keep the cleaned data and analysis reproducible in R.

title: Using Public Data to Guide Sirius Travel Content
text:
Planned analysis
I plan to use:

Descriptive statistics for posting frequency and visible interactions
Comparisons by content theme and format
A time-series chart of Google Trends search interest
A comparison of post timing with periods of higher search interest
A clear explanation that the results show patterns, not proof of cause and effect

title: Using Public Data to Guide Sirius Travel Content
text:
Planned visualizations

Line chart of search interest over time
Bar chart comparing public interaction across content themes
Chart of posting frequency by theme or platform
Summary table connecting findings to content recommendations

title: Using Public Data to Guide Sirius Travel Content
text:
Expected impact
The goal is to give Sirius Travel a clearer basis for deciding what to post and when to post it. The results could help the team plan content around periods of higher search interest.

title: Using Public Data to Guide Sirius Travel Content
text:
Limitations and privacy

Public interactions do not measure bookings or revenue.
Platform metrics may not be directly comparable.
A small sample will limit the conclusions I can make.




Public data only


I will not use customer records, booking data, private analytics, or other nonpublic information.

title: Using Public Data to Guide Sirius Travel Content
text:
Final deliverable
After I collect and analyze the data, the final presentation will show the cleaning process, charts, findings, limitations, and content recommendations.
